result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.cmty_leiden_levels()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Return the community partition at each level of the Leiden algorithm. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.cmty_leiden_levels()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Return the community partition at each level of the Leiden algorithm. title: >- [Graph.cmty_leiden_levels()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Return the community partition at each level of the Leiden algorithm. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Return the community partition at each level of the Leiden algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L36423-L36471){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.cmty_leiden_levels( resolution=1.0, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Leiden community levels](/assets/graphs/cmty-leiden-levels.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A two-by-four ladder, A to D on top and E to H below. Left, Leiden's first level (seed 0) pairs neighbors along the rails into four communities, A, B in the accent color, C, D in teal, E, F in violet and G, H in gold. Right, after refinement and aggregation the next level merges them into two communities, A, B, E, F (accent) and C, D, G, H (teal)." width="100%"} Like `cmty_louvain_levels()`, but for one Leiden run: after each round of local moving the communities are refined (so that every community stays well connected) and aggregated, giving a hierarchy of increasingly coarse partitions. `cmty_leiden()` keeps only the final partition (and repeats runs until modularity stops improving). The graph must be undirected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Resolution parameter (default 1); larger values favor smaller communities. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[dict[int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One node-to-community dictionary per level, finest first. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each level is local moving, refinement and aggregation of the refined partition (Traag, Waltman and van Eck, 2019); the recorded partition is the moved (unrefined) one, mapped back to the original nodes. Mirrors NetworkX's `leiden_partitions`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#b8505c3a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_smallworld_graph(n=60, k=4, p=0.05, seed=1) levels = g.cmty_leiden_levels(seed=2) [len(set(level.values())) for level in levels] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [15, 9, 7] ``` ::: :::
